policy: Every third-party connection candidate declares, before it may be requested or stored: the least-privilege scope set this platform needs, the authority it must never hold, a token retention ceiling, a revocation procedure with a deadline, and the re-authorization reasons a caller must be able to surface. No candidate is published automatically: `allowlist.entries` is empty, `src/http/integrations/boundary.test.ts` asserts `/integrations/*` answers 404, and a promotion ticket must record the owner's allowlist entry in the same PR. Authority: Issue #464.
why_not_a_secret_store: No token value appears in this ledger. The ledger declares scope NAMES, retention and procedure; values live in Infisical (ADR-0015 §1) and are never written into a tracked file, a report row, or a screenshot.

allowlist.rule: A candidate may be published — a mounted `/integrations/*` route, a token requested from the provider, or any automated acceptance of a grant — only after the repository owner records an entry here. The default is an empty list, and an empty list with a mounted route is an error, not a warning.

integrations.grant_note: GitHub OAuth app token. It carries no expiry by default, so the retention ceiling below is ours, not the provider's.

least_privilege.justification: The only GitHub read this platform has ever needed is the authenticated owner's public identity and public events, which `read:user` covers. Repository content, workflow files, packages and organisation administration are capabilities no current obligation owns (`docs/domain/integrations.md` promotes nothing), so requesting them would grant authority that cannot be justified in review and cannot be un-seen by the user.

token_retention.storage: Infisical (ADR-0015 §1 is the source of truth). Never `wrangler.jsonc`, never D1, never a repo file.
token_retention.provider_expiry: none by default for an OAuth app token; a fine-grained token's expiry is an alternative, not a substitute for the ceiling below
token_retention.refresh: interactive re-authorization; an OAuth app token has no refresh token, so there is no unattended renewal path to abuse

triggers: the integration stops being needed (demotion per `docs/domain/integrations.md`)
a credential-shaped string is ever found in the tracked tree
the least-privilege review reports any refusal for a stored grant
the owner is no longer the only person with access to the repository
procedure: revoke the grant in GitHub (Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps → the app → Revoke)
delete the token value in Infisical and re-check the coverage gate
update `status` here and in `docs/domain/integrations.md` to match

triggers: the grant is revoked
the provider answers 401 / invalid_grant
the token is older than the retention ceiling
the issue date was never recorded or cannot be parsed
reauth.surface: the review verdict `reauth_required`; a future handler maps it to `403` plus the reason code

grant_constraints.note: GitHub expresses authority as scope strings, so there is no second constraint block. A GitHub App installation token is NOT an equivalent grant: it carries repository permissions instead, and needs its own reviewed requirement before it may be accepted.

source.note: Scope names and their meanings are taken from the vendor's published scope reference; re-verify before any promotion.

integrations.grant_note: Notion's public-integration OAuth flow returns no scope string. Authority is expressed as per-workspace page/database capabilities the user ticks in the Notion UI, so this ledger reviews the capability list with the same vocabulary it reviews OAuth scopes.

least_privilege.justification: A read-only capability needs exactly `read_content`; `read_user_information` only matters for attributing content to a person, which no current obligation does. `insert_content` is the write capability, and no Notion obligation in `docs/domain/integrations.md` owns a write, so accepting a token that carries it would grant authority nobody reviewed.

token_retention.storage: Infisical (ADR-0015 §1 is the source of truth). Never `wrangler.jsonc`, never D1, never a repo file.
token_retention.provider_expiry: none — a Notion OAuth token stays valid until it is revoked or the connection is removed from the workspace
token_retention.refresh: interactive re-authorization; Notion issues no refresh token

revocation.owner: repository owner, acting in the Notion workspace that granted the connection
triggers: the portfolio/activity capability that needed Notion is dropped
a credential-shaped string is ever found in the tracked tree
the least-privilege review reports any refusal for a stored grant
the workspace owner leaves the team
procedure: remove the connection in the workspace settings (Settings → Connections → the integration → Remove)
delete the token value in Infisical and re-check the coverage gate
update `status` here and in `docs/domain/integrations.md` to match

triggers: the connection was removed or revoked in the workspace
the granted page/database no longer includes the shared page
the token is older than the retention ceiling
the issue date was never recorded or cannot be parsed
reauth.surface: the review verdict `reauth_required`; a future handler maps it to `403` plus the reason code

grant_constraints.note: Because the capability list is per-connection rather than per-app, a grant may also carry capability names this ledger has never reviewed. Those are refused as `scope_outside_review` rather than accepted, which is the behaviour that keeps a Notion workspace's tick-boxes from becoming our policy.

source.note: Capability names come from the vendor's authorization documentation; re-verify before any promotion.

integrations.grant_note: Discord expresses authority twice: OAuth2 scopes on the grant, and a permission integer on a bot invite. Both are reviewed here; the integer is not derivable from the scope list.

least_privilege.justification: `identify` is the smallest scope that can answer "who authorized this connection". Guild membership, message content, RPC and widget scopes each open a surface no current obligation owns, and `email` would collect an address this platform has no reason to hold.

token_retention.storage: Infisical (ADR-0015 §1 is the source of truth). Never `wrangler.jsonc`, never D1, never a repo file.
token_retention.provider_expiry: none — a Discord access token stays valid until it is revoked or the authorization is removed
token_retention.refresh: Discord issues a refresh token; it is stored with the same ceiling and expires the connection with the access token rather than renewing it forever

revocation.owner: repository owner, acting as the Discord user or application that granted the authorization
triggers: the capability that needed Discord is dropped
a credential-shaped string is ever found in the tracked tree
the least-privilege review reports any refusal for a stored grant
the bot is removed from the guild
procedure: revoke the authorization in Discord (User Settings → Connections → the app → Remove, or the OAuth2 app's authorization list)
remove the bot from the guild with the permission integer reset to the allowlist below
delete the token value in Infisical and re-check the coverage gate
update `status` here and in `docs/domain/integrations.md` to match

triggers: the authorization was revoked
the provider answers 401
the token is older than the retention ceiling (Discord tokens are short-lived in practice, so this fires first)
the issue date was never recorded or cannot be parsed
reauth.surface: the review verdict `reauth_required`; a future handler maps it to `403` plus the reason code

grant_constraints.note: Discord permission bits, not scopes: 1024 = ViewChannel (the only bit a read-only surface may hold), 8 = Administrator, 32 = ManageGuild, 268435456 = ManageRoles, 536870912 = ManageWebhooks. Any other bit in an invite integer is refused as unreviewed authority; adding a bit to the allowlist is an owner decision recorded here, not a code change.

source.note: Scope names come from the vendor's OAuth2 documentation and the permission bits from its permissions reference; re-verify before any promotion.

integrations.deferred_reason: No billing / checkout obligation exists in the current product scope (AGENTS.md §11 keeps product feature work out of scope, and `docs/domain/integrations.md` makes "billing enters product scope" the promotion condition). With no capability to scope, the only honest row is one that says no Stripe token may exist yet, and the row itself is what makes that true: a `review: deferred` candidate projects NO requirement into the adapter (`toRequirement()` returns `null`), so a grant naming `stripe` answers `unknown_integration`, and the gate errors if this row grows a `least_privilege` or `token_retention` block while the marker stays (probe `deferred-with-requirement.json`). The `stripe-deferred-no-requirement` connection below measures that claim instead of asserting it. Review this row before any billing ticket requests a token.

reviewed_connections.scenario: the one connection this Issue validates end to end: exactly the reviewed scope, inside the retention ceiling
a consent screen that asked for repository write too — the unapproved scope has to be visible
a long-lived token that drifted past the 90-day ceiling
the workspace ticked the write capability as well
a capability this ledger has never reviewed is refused rather than assumed harmless
the smallest Discord grant that answers who authorized the connection
a grant that also reads guild membership and an e-mail address
a well-scoped grant that was revoked — re-authorization, not a scope refusal
a Discord token older than its 30-day ceiling
the deferred candidate, executed rather than described: a grant naming it has no reviewed requirement, so it is refused as unknown — not as over-scoped, and not as missing a retention ceiling
